info.description:
Machine-readable contract for the Culvert admin/control-plane REST API served
on the UI port (`-ui-port`, default 9090).

**Scope.** This document describes the HTTP/JSON admin API only. Two other
Culvert network surfaces are intentionally NOT modelled here because they are
not RESTful and OpenAPI cannot describe them faithfully:

  * the forward-proxy data path (HTTP CONNECT / plain-HTTP forward / SOCKS5)
    served on `-port` — a proxy protocol, not a resource API;
  * the Control-Plane ↔ Data-Plane gRPC stream — described by protobuf.

**Accuracy over aspiration.** Every operation, schema, status code, and
content type below reflects the *actual* runtime behavior of the handler, not
a target design. Notably, error responses are currently emitted by
`http.Error` as `text/plain`; that is documented as-is here. The proposed
structured JSON error envelope is a *future* target recorded in
docs/api/API-STYLE-GUIDE.md and the consistency risk register — it is NOT yet
the runtime behavior and therefore is NOT asserted by this contract.

**Air-gap.** This appliance and its documentation are designed for on-prem,
internet-isolated deployment. No operation here depends on an external
service, and the rendered documentation vendors all assets locally.

This baseline (contract version 1.0.0) documents a representative,
security-spanning subset of operations. The remaining registered routes are
explicitly classified — and time-boxed for documentation — in
api/route-classification.yaml, which the route-coverage CI gate enforces
against the live router.

post.description:
Forces a CA rotation using a two-step confirmation-token flow: the first
POST returns `{status:"pending_confirmation", confirmation_token}` and
emits a `ca.rotate_requested` audit event; re-POSTing with the token
applies the rotation and emits `ca.rotate`. Re-signs future leaf
certificates under a new root; clients that pinned the previous root will
fail until they re-trust. Admin-only and audited.

confirm.description: Set true on the second step to apply the rotation.

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the first (request) step.

requestBody.description:
Omit (or send `{}`) on the first step to request rotation and receive a
token. On the second step send `{confirm:true, confirmation_token}` with
the token from the first response to apply the rotation.

200.description:
Rotation requested (`status:pending_confirmation` with a token) or
applied, depending on whether a valid confirmation token was supplied.

500.description: Rotation failed. Body is plain text.
